title: How Mukesh Ambani built Jio
description: The 31-beat Jio v2 cut. Placeholder cameras mark shots awaiting production.

narration.style: fast, punchy, confident YouTube Shorts explainer narrator, playful and a little cheeky
script: Imagine you're Mukesh Ambani. You own refineries, petrol pumps and plastics. But you lost the one business your father dreamed of.
In 2002, your father Dhirubhai wanted a phone call to cost less than a postcard.
Then the family splits the empire. Your brother Anil gets the phone company, and you promise to stay out of telecom.
So you watch.
In 2015, most Indians are online on slow 2G.
One gigabyte costs about 250 rupees,
and every video buffers forever.
Airtel, Vodafone and Idea make their money on voice calls. So data stays a luxury.
But you see something they don't.
In 2010, your deal with Anil ends.
Weeks later, an unknown company called Infotel wins 4G airwaves in all 22 circles.
Within hours, you buy 95 percent of it.
Then your daughter Isha comes home from Yale and says, "Dad, the internet in our house sucks."
Your son Akash adds: telecom isn't about calls anymore. It's about data.
So you decide: data should be like oxygen. Cheap enough for everyone.
You don't fix the old towers. You build India's first 4G-only network, where even calls travel as data.
You lay three lakh kilometres of fibre.
The bill: one and a half lakh crore rupees. You call it the world's biggest startup.
On September 5th, 2016, you launch Jio. And everything is free. Calls. Data. Apps.
Sixteen million people join in 26 days.
A hundred million in 170 days. That's seven new customers every second.
Your rivals run to the regulator, crying predatory pricing. You say their networks are dropping your calls.
And the insane part? You even give away the phone. The JioPhone, at an effective price of zero.
Data crashes from 250 rupees a gigabyte to under 20.
India becomes the world's biggest consumer of mobile data.
Telenor exits. Tata exits. Aircel goes bankrupt. Even your brother's company shuts down. Vodafone and Idea merge just to survive.
By 2019, Jio is number one.
Then Facebook pays 5.7 billion dollars for a slice. Google pays 4.5 billion.
Today, 524 million Indians are on Jio.
Your father wanted a phone call cheaper than a postcard. You made it free.
That's why you call it Jio. In Hindi, it means "live".
